notes:
The background video in distraction-free mode no longer stops for good. It could be paused by the system at any moment - when another window covered Corylus, when a piece of the file was slow to arrive, or when memory ran short - and nothing ever started it again, so the only cure was leaving distraction-free mode and coming back. It now notices and resumes on its own, and writes down why it stopped.

A dropped connection no longer breaks cloud sync for the rest of the day. A transfer interrupted by a lost network could keep running invisibly and hold the remote folder open, so every sync afterwards queued behind it and timed out - for hours, without a word. Corylus now spots that, stops trying, tells you plainly that the project is not syncing, and gives you a button to start it again. Losing the network for a moment is also reported as being offline, which it is, instead of as an error.

When something goes wrong behind the scenes, the reason is now written down. Until now a whole class of failures recorded the words \u201cobject Object\u201d and nothing else, which meant a problem could repeat hundreds of times in a day and leave no trace of its cause.
